takeaway: Difficulty standing and walking after a groin stab wound: femoral nerve injury. Largest branch of the lumbar plexus (L2-4); passes behind the inguinal ligament, lateral to the femoral sheath.

lines.text: An 18-year-old man is stabbed in the groin and the abdomen.
lines.say: An eighteen year old man is stabbed in the groin and the abdomen.

lines.text: Three months later, he finds standing and walking difficult.
This is due to damage to the femoral nerve.
It is the largest branch of the lumbar plexus, from the posterior roots of L2, 3 and 4.
lines.say: It is the largest branch of the lumbar plexus, from the posterior roots of L two, three and four.

lines.text: After a motor branch to iliacus, it passes behind the inguinal ligament.
In the femoral triangle it lies lateral to the femoral sheath.
There, the lateral femoral circumflex artery divides it into superficial and deep branches.
